summary: `kuna disassemble` now reports, always, the addresses its own instructions branch or call to that no row of its listing starts at -- the tell that a straight-line decode is a byte out of phase, which is otherwise spelled exactly like a correct one. The new `--follow` flag additionally decodes from those addresses, to a fixpoint over whatever the newly decoded rows themselves name, and fills what flow never reaches with the ordinary straight-line walk between the anchored rows.

decisions.what: hypothesis UPHELD, and all four of the round-12 refuter's corrections were load-bearing
decisions.detail: The filed cause ('the linear sweep does not diagnose instructions covering direct branch targets') is exactly right and the refuter had already proved it at the code level: `kuna disassemble` has three note producers (choose_view's data-section note, pool_note, image_bound_note) and none is branch-aware. Its four corrections are all carried: (1) THREE targets, not one -- 0x43d092, 0x43d0ae, 0x43d0c1, which is what the shipped note prints; (2) the harm is the FABRICATED rows, not the missing one, which is what the note text and the PR body lead with; (3) a one-shot restart is not a fix -- 0x43d092's own next instruction is another EB 01, so the follow walk is a fixpoint; (4) the acceptance was tightened to name 0x43d092 before dispatch, and the shipped note satisfies it.

decisions.what: the diagnostic is always on; only the follow walk is a flag
decisions.detail: An agent cannot infer a desynchronized decode from the output -- that is the whole defect -- so the note must not be behind anything. It is also not spam: swept over ~800 functions of every vendored fixture it fires on 8, and all 8 are real (the row covering the target is `00ff ADD BH,BH` / `0031` / `12e8 ADC CH,AL` -- run-on decodes of padding at the extent edge). The follow walk costs a second decode and changes which bytes are read as which instruction, so it is opt-in.

decisions.what: the evidence was already being collected; nothing new is decoded for the note
decisions.detail: `FixedRefs::flow_targets` is harvested per row for the literal-pool fold (`add_fixed_refs_at`). `skipped_targets` is one filter over it: in the listed span, not a row start. Cost is one BTreeSet of row addresses per listing.

decisions.what: one measured fall-through rule decides whether the follow walk works at all
decisions.detail: The first follow implementation reproduced the linear listing exactly, because the run stopped at 0x43d067 `CALL 0x43d06c`. Dumping the p-code showed [INT_SUB, STORE, BRANCH], not CALL: Ghidra's x86 spec gives `E8 00000000` -- the get-PC idiom every packer stub opens with -- its own constructor `:CALL rel32 is ... simm32=0 & rel32 { push24(&:4 inst_next); goto rel32; }` (ia.sinc:2969). `harvest` therefore treats a final BRANCH whose destination IS the fall-through address as falling through, alongside the constant-space (p-code-relative) case. Without that clause the walk dies at the first instruction of the witness.

decisions.what: --follow must never list less than the straight line, and two early versions did
decisions.detail: A whole-fixture sweep caught both. (a) On ARM the gap decode started with no alignment witness, so a refused byte resumed one byte later and every row after it was off the 4-byte grid -- 9 invented instructions in entrymain_arm. Fixed by seeding `decode_rows` with the OR of the claimed rows' addresses and sizes. (b) The gap and claim clips used the window's own end as a ceiling, so the last row of a --follow listing was clipped where the straight line lists the instruction straddling the end whole (macho_objc). Fixed by clipping only on claimed rows and on mapped memory. After both, the sweep goes from 33 differing listings to 2.

decisions.what: rows may overlap under --follow, and that is the answer, not a bug
decisions.detail: In overlapbranch_i386 a `JNZ 0x8048825` jumps into the middle of the 5-byte CALL at 0x8048824, and both readings are reachable: the fall-through path executes the CALL, the taken path executes `ADD EAX,0x7`. --follow lists both rows. Dropping either would be a guess about which path runs. Documented in docs/cli.md and the module header; only --follow can produce it.

decisions.what: no option, no phases.toml row, no catalog counter, no stages XML
decisions.detail: Driver tier: the change is entirely in kuna-cli's listing surface plus one derived bit on kuna-console's FixedRefs. A listing is a query -- nothing is committed into the engine and no emitted C can move, which `make test` 675/675 and `make test-stages` PARITY OK confirm. The stage/datatest corpora are XML <binaryimage> documents that never reach this surface. A DIV row IS required, because the always-on note is an intentional default-behaviour change.

sweep.question: does --follow ever produce a listing that is WRONG, or the note ever fire where nothing is wrong?
sweep.method: `kuna disassemble <fn>` with and without `--follow` for up to 8 functions of every file under decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures and tests/hang-repro -- ~800 functions across x86, x86-64, i386 PE, x86-64 PE, ARM A32/Thumb, Mach-O (x86-64 and arm64), MIPS16, PPC64LE and RISC-V -- diffing the text listings and counting the skipped-target notes.
sweep.result: 2 listings differ, both anti-disassembly cases and both improvements: jumpoverdecoy_i386 (the vendored witness reduction -- LODSB/STOSB/LOOP recovered where the straight line printed CALL and an out-of-image JMP) and overlapbranch_i386 (recovers `ADD EAX,0x7` at 0x8048825, hidden inside the CALL its JNZ jumps over). Every other listing is byte-identical. The note fires on 8 of ~800: crtmain_x86_64.exe, jumpoverdecoy_i386, overlapbranch_i386, pe_cookiecheck_x86_64.exe, pe_headercode_i386.exe, pe_iatincode_i386.exe, unmapped_call_x86_64, win32sigs_pe_i386.exe -- each one a call target the last row of the listing runs across, with a fabricated row over it.
sweep.earlier_arm: The same sweep on the first implementation reported 33 differing listings; the two clip/alignment defects it exposed are in `decisions` above and were fixed before this run.
